findings.summary: The static Dockerfile test accepts USER 00, USER 0000 and USER +0, which Docker reads as root; the real Dockerfile uses 10001.
The named-paths-only check misses COPY ./. ./, COPY .* ./ and COPY ** ./; the real Dockerfile uses none.
The image file checker compares names case-sensitively and scans line by line, so an upper-case env-file name or a credential split over two lines is missed.
The ignore file for the image build has no pattern for SQLite database files; the checker would still refuse one in the image.
The human task file names a dependency-install stage the Dockerfile does not have, and step 4 says the risk is none where the template asks what would print if the rule fails.
No CI run shows the wrong-Python-minor refusal; only the static test does.
